OPENING_CONTRIBUTED_BASIS.plain_language: Capital the owner had already contributed when governed daily tracking begins; it is not the account market value.
OPENING_CONTRIBUTED_BASIS.calculation_effect: Add the admitted opening basis once on the accepted funding or membership start date; missing evidence makes the interval incomplete.
examples: A strategy begins governed tracking with an evidenced 100000 contributed basis; invested capital starts at 100000 even if market value differs.

IN_KIND_FUNDING.plain_language: Securities or other assets transferred into the portfolio instead of cash.
IN_KIND_FUNDING.calculation_effect: Increase invested capital by the admitted value at the flow time; missing valuation or required FX evidence makes the interval incomplete.
examples: Transferring shares worth 25000 from an owner-held outside account into a governed strategy would add 25000 without a cash deposit.

EXTERNAL_CONTRIBUTION.plain_language: Cash supplied by the owner that crosses from outside the governed portfolio into it.
EXTERNAL_CONTRIBUTION.calculation_effect: Increase strategy and aggregate invested capital by the admitted base-currency amount.
examples: An owner deposit of 10000 increases invested capital by 10000.

EXTERNAL_WITHDRAWAL.plain_language: Cash or property that leaves the governed portfolio and is returned to the owner.
EXTERNAL_WITHDRAWAL.calculation_effect: Decrease strategy and aggregate invested capital by the admitted base-currency amount.
examples: An owner withdrawal of 7000 decreases invested capital by 7000.

INTERNAL_TRANSFER.plain_language: Capital moved between two strategies or accounts that are both inside the governed portfolio.
INTERNAL_TRANSFER.calculation_effect: Decrease the sending strategy and increase the receiving strategy by equal admitted amounts; aggregate invested capital is unchanged and an unpaired transfer is rejected.
examples: Moving 5000 from strategy A to strategy B changes each strategy by minus or plus 5000 and changes the portfolio aggregate by zero.

DIVIDEND_INTEREST_REINVESTMENT.plain_language: Income produced by holdings and any purchase made by reinvesting that same portfolio income; no new owner capital crosses the boundary.
DIVIDEND_INTEREST_REINVESTMENT.calculation_effect: Leave invested capital unchanged because income and reinvestment are portfolio performance, which the MVP definition excludes.
examples: A 200 dividend paid and reinvested changes holdings and NAV but not invested capital.

FEE_TAX_REBATE_EXPENSE.plain_language: Operating charges, taxes, expenses, or refunds recorded in or around the portfolio.
FEE_TAX_REBATE_EXPENSE.calculation_effect: Internal fees, taxes, expenses, and rebates remain investment results and do not change invested capital; separately evidenced cash crossing between owner and portfolio follows the external-flow rule.
examples: A broker fee deducted inside the account has no effect; owner cash injected to pay a charge is an external contribution.

MARGIN_FINANCING.plain_language: Money borrowed from or repaid to a broker or lender, including related financing activity.
MARGIN_FINANCING.calculation_effect: Debt proceeds and repayments do not become owner invested capital. Leverage, gross exposure, liabilities, financing cost, NAV, total return, TWR, MWR, HWM, decomposition, and dependence retain the leveraged economics.
examples: Borrowing 30000 on margin increases cash and debt but not owner invested capital.

PREDECESSOR_TRANSITION.plain_language: Capital moved from a prior General bucket, predecessor strategy, or old strategy identity into a current strategy, including a pure rename or remap.
PREDECESSOR_TRANSITION.calculation_effect: A same-perimeter transition reallocates invested capital by strategy with zero aggregate effect; an evidenced boundary crossing is treated as external funding or withdrawal, and an unproved transition remains incomplete.
examples: Renaming General to strategy A does not create new aggregate capital; importing a previously outside account may do so if the boundary crossing is evidenced.

CORRECTION_REVERSAL.plain_language: A ledger event that cancels or corrects an earlier admitted event; duplicate events are repeated records of the same economic action.
CORRECTION_REVERSAL.calculation_effect: A source correction restates the original effective date without rewriting an accepted generation, while a later economic reversal changes invested capital on its own provider event date; duplicate economic events are rejected.
examples: Correcting an erroneous 10000 contribution replaces the original event in a new generation; a later real return of that 10000 is a withdrawal on the later event date.

flow_timing.plain_language: The effective date and within-day ordering that determine which daily invested-capital point contains a flow and how the same flow aligns with return and HWM calculations.
flow_timing.calculation_effect: The admitted timestamp determines the exact boundary; a date-only flow enters at end of day and carries INFERRED_TIMING. The choice changes same-day capital weights or return compatibility but not the eventual cumulative amount.
examples: A contribution dated Monday may appear in Monday end-of-day capital but must not be silently treated as capital that earned all of Monday return.

fx_base_currency.plain_language: The single reporting currency used to add flows across accounts, plus the accepted exchange-rate observation used for a non-base-currency event.
fx_base_currency.calculation_effect: Every admitted non-USD flow is converted to USD at the accepted event-time rate; USD-native facts use conversion one, and missing currency or exact FX authority makes the affected interval incomplete.
examples: A EUR contribution is converted once using the accepted event-date EUR-to-base rate before entering invested capital.

negative_net_contributions.plain_language: The case where cumulative withdrawals exceed opening basis plus cumulative contributions, so the signed net external capital becomes less than zero.
negative_net_contributions.calculation_effect: Invested capital remains a faithful signed net-flow measure; it is not a negative account value and does not classify the excess withdrawal as a gain.
examples: If total contributed basis is 100000 and cumulative withdrawals are 120000, signed net invested capital is minus 20000.
